Koh Samui is best known for full-service wellness resorts on the quieter south-east and north-east coasts, plus cliffside yoga between Chaweng Noi and Coral Cove. In 2026, retreats run from donation-based silent meditation courses in the hills above Lamai, through all-inclusive yoga weeks from about US$650 for 3 nights, to medical-style detox programmes of US$2,000–5,000 a week. The driest months are February to April; October to December is the rainy season, though covered shalas keep most retreats running all year. Tell us what you are looking for and we'll help you choose and arrange transfers and boat days around it.

Yoga retreats

Yoga retreats on Samui combine a room, daily classes and healthy meals, usually for 3–14 nights. Most welcome beginners; the main differences are intensity, food rules and how remote the setting is. Classes mix hatha, vinyasa and yin, with pranayama and meditation; fitness-focused retreats add strength sessions, Pilates or Muay Thai.

  1. 07:00 Morning practice: breathing and a 90-minute flow class in an open-air shala.
  2. 09:30 Brunch, then free time: beach, pool or a massage.
  3. 14:00 Workshop or private session (alignment, inversions, anatomy) on some days.
  4. 16:30 Yin or restorative class as the heat drops.
  5. 18:30 Dinner and an early night, or an evening meditation.

Timetables differ by host; the day above is typical of Samui's yoga retreats rather than a specific schedule. Compare venues in our yoga guide.

Meditation retreats

Silent retreats ask you to stop talking, hand in or switch off your phone, get up before dawn and follow a timetable of sitting and walking meditation, with simple vegetarian food. Guided or resort-based meditation is gentler: sessions sit alongside yoga, spa and free time. On Samui, Dipabhavan in the Maret hills runs donation-based silent courses in the Suan Mokkh tradition, and the Samui International Meditation Center in Bophut offers monk-led residential retreats of about a week. On the mainland, Suan Mokkh's International Dharma Hermitage near Chaiya runs a 10-day silent retreat from the 1st to the 11th of every month for 2,000 THB, with in-person registration on the last day of the previous month. Rules, etiquette and how to register are in meditation on Koh Samui.

Detox and wellness programmes

Samui's wellness resorts run structured programmes that start with a consultation and body-composition analysis, then combine nutrition (often juice or plant-based menus), treatments, fitness and rest. Kamalaya's run from a 3-night Relax and Renew (about US$1,836) to a 7–14-night Comprehensive Detox with full board (from about US$4,867), and Absolute Sanctuary's from a 6-night Be Fit package (about US$2,152) to a 31-night Lifestyle Change. If you take regular medication, are pregnant or have diabetes, heart, kidney or liver disease or a history of eating disorders, see your doctor before any fasting or detox programme. Full comparison: detox and wellness resorts.

Healing and spa retreats

Spa-led retreats centre on treatments rather than exercise: daily massages, herbal compresses and steam, lymphatic drainage, Ayurvedic therapies and facials. Kamalaya's Asian Bliss programme (Ayurveda, 5–10 nights) and Absolute Sanctuary's Rest and Balance and Sleep Well programmes fall into this group. For a do-it-yourself version, combine daily Thai massages (about 300–500 THB an hour at good shops) with sessions in the herbal steam caves at Tamarind Springs (1,500 THB++). To learn Thai massage yourself, several schools and spas on the island teach short courses; ask us for current dates. Prices and tips are in our spa and massage guide.

How to choose a retreat

  • Goal first: rest, fitness, weight, sleep, spiritual practice or a qualification? The right host follows from that.
  • Structure: do you want a fixed timetable, or a flexible stay with classes you can skip?
  • Food and alcohol: detox and temple retreats are strict; yoga retreats vary; wellness resorts leave it partly to you.
  • Room: shared or private, air-conditioned or fan, sea view or garden. Solo travellers should ask about single supplements.
  • Medical support: for detox and fasting, ask who supervises and what happens if you feel unwell.
  • Location: the south coast is beautiful and remote; the north-east is close to the airport, restaurants and boat piers.
  • Total cost: ask for a written, itemised quote including service charge, VAT, transfers and extra treatments.

Private group retreats

Teachers and groups often run their own retreat in a large pool villa: 6–10-bedroom villas cost about 30,000–120,000 THB a night for the whole house in the low season. Check that the terrace or garden is big and flat enough for mats, that events are allowed, and that a cook can be arranged. We can add airport transfers, a private van for excursions and a private boat day for the group.

What to pack

  • Light, modest clothing (covering shoulders and knees for temple retreats).
  • Practice clothes and a towel; most hosts provide mats.
  • Insect repellent, reef-safe sunscreen, a hat and a refillable water bottle.
  • A light rain jacket from October to December.
  • Any regular medication, plus a letter from your doctor if you are joining a detox programme.

How booking works

  1. Message us on WhatsApp with your dates, budget and the kind of retreat you want.
  2. We suggest options that fit and check availability for your dates.
  3. Retreat programmes are quoted individually, and each host's deposit and cancellation terms are sent to you in writing before you pay.
  4. We can add airport transfers, a private van for days out and boat trips around your programme. Our own tours follow our standard cancellation policy.

Prices are charged in THB. We confirm by email or WhatsApp after payment.

Getting to your retreat and visas

Samui International Airport (USM) has about 20–25 flights a day from Bangkok Suvarnabhumi (about 1 hour 10 minutes) plus flights from Singapore and Hong Kong. A taxi from the airport costs about 400–700 THB depending on the zone; retreats in the south are 45 minutes away, so ask your host about transfers or book a private van. Overland, budget travellers fly to Surat Thani and take a coach and ferry (5–7 hours in total). See how to get to Koh Samui.

Since 15 September 2026 most nationalities get 30 days visa-free, extendable once by 30 days at Samui immigration in Maenam (1,900 THB). Every arrival must file the free digital arrival card at tdac.immigration.go.th within 3 days before landing. For a month or more, see the DTV in our Thailand visa guide.

Combine a retreat with a day on the water

Most programmes leave a free day, and the sea is the best way to spend it. The Pig Island sunset tour (1,550 THB, 5–6 hours with dinner) and the half-day Pig Island speedboat (1,450 THB) run every day of the year. From 16 December, the boutique yachting day to Ang Thong Marine Park on a wooden gulet costs 4,500 THB with the park fee included. Hotel pickup is included from most areas of Koh Samui. Nathon, Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao and Thong Krut (and other remote areas) add 400 THB per person, return; zones vary by pier, so check each product. For groups running their own retreat, a private pool villa with a shala-sized terrace is often the best base.
